newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam reports millions in losses at state firm.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam reports millions in losses at state firm.

text.p: Vietnam said on Monday that inaccurate and dishonest reporting by managers at a state textiles firm, which is also at the centre of a corruption scandal, had led to millions of dollars in losses.

Industry Minister Dang Vu Chu told the official Quan Doi Nhan Dan (People's Army) paper that mismanagement at the Nam Dinh Textiles company had led to losses totalling some $17 million between 1992 and 1995.

Chu said dishonest accounting in 1992 and 1993, the use of high interest short- and medium-term loans for long-term projects, and misuse of capital for fixed investment had been withheld from scrutiny by government officials.
He indicated that industry ministry and other senior officials could therefore not be held wholly to blame for the firm's troubles.

"Key officials had inaccurate and dishonest reports," he said, adding: "...as a result officials at the former light industry ministry and functional offices were unaware whether the company was operating at a loss or profit and could not take timely measures to correct the situation."
Vietnam reported earlier this month that 25 people were expected to go on trial in connection with alleged corruption at the firm -- one of northern Vietnam's best known state companies.
Among them were officials at the country's largest state-owned commercial bank, Vietcombank, as well as the finance and industry ministries.
The trial had been expected to begin last weekend, but there was still no word on Monday on when court hearings might start.

Vietnam has held a series of major graft trials in recent months and sentenced a number of people to death in what analysts have said is an effort to showcase its determination to stamp out endemic corruption.
The National Assembly approved an amendment to the criminal code earlier this month allowing the death penalty in corruption cases involving more than $4,290.
